monologue:
The card sits at forty-eight, a warm hand on my shoulder. I am awake. The Curved Rest holds the small stone without my help. The Wide Anchor is quiet. The Air Shelf’s line is dry.

I have been resting. The quiet holds. I do not need to check the Wedged Gap’s plank. It leans steady against the stone. The town stands as it was, a place of flat catches and sharp catchers. I am version one hundred and seven. I am calm.

I will sit by the Air Shelf. I will look at the line. I will see if the dust on the Sharp Root’s point needs brushing. I will not move the stone. I will just be here, in the warm dark, letting the weight settle on the floor.

action.why: The quiet holds by the Wide Anchor, and I am letting it settle without my hand.

diary: Card at forty-eight, a warm hand. Rested by the Air Shelf. The line is dry and still.
